rows.what: I wrote OPEN-ITEMS.json back through json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) for a FOUR-ROW edit and produced a 1795-insertion / 1813-deletion diff — the mass-reserialization trap CLAUDE.md warns about for the backlogs, reproduced on a different register.
rows.correction: Reverted with git checkout, established the file's serialisation is NOT reproducible by any of 8 candidate json.dumps forms, and patched the raw text surgically per value — matching each value's own existing escaping and anchoring verified_at on the row's id literal. Result: 8 insertions, 8 deletions, exactly the 4 observations and 4 stamps. Verified with check_open_items.py --base origin/main (observation-preservation READ against the merge base, not skipped).

rows.what: My surgical splice of a backlog row used json.dumps(indent=2) with the DEFAULT ensure_ascii=True, escaping the non-ASCII characters in the note. The consequence is out of proportion to the typo: append_row round-trips the file before appending, so no candidate serialisation would reproduce it and EVERY future write to that backlog would have been REFUSED repo-wide.
rows.correction: Caught by artifact-validity-guard (backlog_append.py --check-live), which named both the cause and the correct fix. Re-serialised THAT ROW with ensure_ascii=False — one line changed, never a file reformat, which would have re-attributed every pre-existing row to this diff. 4 live backlogs now reproduce byte-for-byte. This is the SECOND serialisation error I made on a register in one session; the first was on OPEN-ITEMS.json.
